tldr: Three arXiv papers in five days attack question answering over structured content: tables in document images, knowledge graphs without labeled questions, and multilingual multi-hop documents. All three add structure or self-evaluation around the model instead of relying on a single pass.
whats_new: DocSkill (Oct 27) applies skill-integrated agentic reasoning to multilingual multi-hop document QA, where evidence spans complex layouts, pages and languages.
why_it_matters: Document and KG question answering is a common production RAG workload, and these papers move reliability gains into orchestration (iterative self-checks, skills, self-generated training signal) you can adopt without a new base model.

status.detail: Research-stage papers only; no released code, benchmarks or production results are cited in this thread.

beats.headline: Cycle-of-Thought adds self-evaluation to table VQA
beats.summary: Iterative self-checking targets inconsistent VLM reasoning over tables in document images.

beats.headline: Evolve on Graph trains KG reasoning without question annotations
beats.summary: Aimed at finance and industry KGs that lack QA pairs.

beats.headline: DocSkill brings skills to multilingual multi-hop document QA

open_questions: Do any of the three papers release code or evaluation harnesses that others can reproduce?
Does DocSkill report gains over single-pass baselines on multilingual document benchmarks?
take_for_builders: If you run document or table QA in production, test an iterative self-check pass on your own failure cases before adopting any of these; none shows production-grade evidence yet.
